## Clause (Cl)

The clause library. `name`, `clauseType` (payment / liability / indemnification / termination / confidentiality / data_protection / force_majeure / auto_renewal / other), `standardText` (the approved wording), `riskLevel` (low → critical, the same four grades as the contract's RiskRatingField so one palette serves both), `guidance` (when to use it and what must never be conceded without sign-off), `ownerRole`, `reviewedAt` (approved language goes stale — a first-class date, not metadata).

A Clause is NOT a contract term: it has no parties, dates or value. It is a template fragment. The instance that appears in an agreement is **ContractClause**, which links back here and records `actualText` and `deviationSeverity`; a deviation is precisely "actualText departs from this standardText". Clause Reference (field) pins a document to the revision (`reviewedAt`) it relied on, so re-reviewing the library never rewrites history.

Typed subclasses — Confidentiality Clause, Termination Clause, Payment Clause — adopt from this card, so the library and the Clause Navigator treat them uniformly.

### Formats

isolated (text, guidance, risk, where-used via query), embedded, atom, fitted (attribute-only — prerendered fitted does not resolve links).

### Example

Liability Cap — 12 Months Fees; the Acme MSA deviates from it.

### Non-goals

No text-level diffing (deviation severity is recorded judgment). No versioning of the text itself — re-review updates `reviewedAt`; documents pin to it via Clause Reference.

cardInfo.summary: A pre-approved piece of contract language owned by legal — the reference every ContractClause is measured against; without a library there is no such thing as a deviation.
